title: Building a new path to make medicines with AI
fullText:
Solving all disease is one of the most monumentally complex challenges in science. Today, for the first time, AI provides the foundation to make it achievable.

Tackling the frontier of human health is our mission, and it means identifying exactly where modern AI can make the greatest difference. We see drug discovery as the critical wedge in solving all disease, and therefore our initial focal point where AI can have a transformative impact on human health. Developing a drug that successfully and effectively treats disease fundamentally involves understanding biological mechanisms and designing exquisitely engineered molecules that can modulate them safely.

So we are taking a straight shot at making that a reality. We are generating the data, training the AI models, developing the software, and laying down the physical infrastructure to make new medicines; taking these potential therapeutics all the way to patients in the clinic. We are building this new architecture in a way that will scale across multiple disease areas, and different types of medicines, from small molecules to antibodies, peptides, and beyond.

In 2021, when we started Isomorphic Labs, AI drug discovery was just a hypothesis. Conventional approaches were bottlenecked by slow, resource-intensive iterative design-make-test cycles, viewing AI as an experimental tool for narrow tasks. At the same time the AI revolution was well underway across multiple industries. A seismic shift was happening with the emergence of foundation models, moving away from single-task algorithms toward highly versatile systems capable of world-understanding, zero-shot reasoning and generating complex text and images.

Up to this point, I had spent my education and career in core AI, building intelligent systems by scaling up neural networks and deep reinforcement learning to solve the hardest problems at a superhuman level. But having grown up in a medical family, I recognised the potential to apply this superhuman new technology to humanity’s most meaningful challenge: human health. Working with Sir Demis Hassabis, we created the founding team at Isomorphic Labs to pivot breakthroughs in AI toward solving the drug discovery problem. We set out on a path to approach drug discovery as an engineering process, stripping back to first principles, to rebuild the process to design medicines. Almost every field of engineering has been revolutionised at some point over the last 50 years by computer aided design, but I believe its transformational advancement in the making of medicines has only just begun. We saw a huge opportunity, using AI to fuel the computational methods that will turn this field into a more systematic engineering discipline, ultimately to bring life-changing medicines to patients that need them.

We are moving from empirical medicine toward exquisitely engineered molecules, and AI is the engine driving this shift. By stripping back to first principles, we are building AI to help us understand healthy and disease states at the molecular level. Subsequently we can leverage our superior predictive and generative capabilities to come up with a potentially exquisite molecular design that displays the best functional characteristics before it reaches patients.

Today, AI drug discovery is no longer a hypothesis. The mammoth contribution of AI in protein structure prediction was recognised with a Nobel Prize in 2024 for the work of AlphaFold 2. At Isomorphic Labs, we spent the last half decade building on this advancement and taking it further, creating the Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE). IsoDDE goes beyond structure prediction, to a system with a suite of predictive capabilities that can accelerate the design and pre-clinical development of unique molecules. Our engine continues to exceed all existing deep-learning models and industry-standard computational methods for designing molecules to date. We have reshaped our drug design processes around this new predictive capability.

I want to zoom in to a core capability of our drug design engine: its ability to accelerate the design and optimisation of new drug candidates. The theoretical chemical space to search for small drug-like molecules is vast (people argue around 1060). Conventional experimental methods, like high-throughput library screening, can take months (even years) to evaluate fixed libraries of compounds (105-109) against proteins. To then optimise any initial hits into a clinical candidate involves a multi-year iterative search through chemical space, gradually improving and balancing the many properties required for a molecule to be ready for clinical trials.

In contrast, our drug design engine can intelligently search the chemical space in just a few days on a computer, designing functional molecules ready for the real world. I’m excited to share a snapshot of what that looks like.

The below videos are a representation of the progression of creating new molecule designs with the IsoDDE working autonomously over 2-4 days. Our drug designers input a design specification, a set of criteria and goals for what they want to create: the biological target, the type of molecule and mode of modulation, the required selectivity, and the desired properties of the molecule (e.g. solubility, cell permeability etc). Our design agent batch-iteratively generated molecules and searched the chemical space to improve desirability against our design specification. The green colour represents a desirable search: the greener the colour, the better the molecule.

This video zooms into Target D, illustrating a single search process, dramatically accelerating the path for hit molecule discovery. Traditionally, each step along this path requires 1–3 months of work – manually designing and making these molecules by teams of chemists, testing them by teams of biologists, and iteratively analysing the new data. Our AI drug design agent completes the same progression computationally in days by relying on our frontier AI predictive models rather than going directly to the lab. The agent’s process dynamically balances the exploration of vast, uncharted chemical space with the targeted exploitation of promising scaffolds in this open-ended learning problem. As the agent designs and evaluates candidates, it pushes the multi-objective pareto frontier, which is the optimal boundary where competing properties like potency and bioavailability are balanced. We can see the agent’s internal attention (represented as a heatmap) progress, shifting computational focus: broad attention during early exploration then narrows, to exploit and fine-tune the pareto frontier whilst still maintaining exploration.

At the end of the agent’s optimisation, we select multiple diverse compounds synthesis and then test the final designs to validate in the lab. The image below represents the functional concentration response curve from the real world experimental testing of the output of the molecular search process above, with a literature-derived molecule for reference (estimated result of 3-5 years of work from authors). The experimental curve shows the agent-designed molecule successfully modulates the biological target with good properties, which is a great starting point for designing a potential therapeutic.

What we show above is one example of dozens. From our experience of applying IsoDDE to many problems to date, we have seen we are able to find functional molecules for problems with which others have greatly struggled. We can do so with less real-world lab time, and in novel chemical spaces that have the potential for exquisite properties, and modulating biological mechanisms, those that have never been tried or proven before. Instead of testing thousands to millions of molecules in the real world, we can synthesise just a handful of molecules and get better experimental results. The capabilities from IsoDDE allow us to not only create scientific hypotheses of new molecules, but to do a lot of predictive validation, so that when we do test our hypotheses in the lab they have a much higher chance of success.

Isomorphic Labs started in a one-room office, with a deeply held hypothesis and a handful of the world’s most talented scientists and engineers. At the beginning, our first scientific breakthroughs on our drug discovery programs came slowly. Over the last five years, we’ve worked relentlessly to increase the accuracy and breadth of capabilities, and as a result, the rate of scientific breakthroughs has drastically increased. Using the IsoDDE we’ve uncovered new biological mechanisms, designed molecules that open previously unknown pockets, and have validated wet lab results demonstrating unique biological functionality. Our hypothesis has been proven. Our preclinical data is helping us to gear up for clinical developments. We are pushing with full force to deliver the impact that AI-driven drug design can achieve for patients, to make discovery and development less like magic and more like precise, repeatable engineering. There is no greater privilege than to work on solving this problem, and we are laser-focussed on bringing these results to the people who need them most.

title: Warner Bros/Paramount to change name to Skydance
description: As Hollywood's big five studios become the big three-and-a-half, CEO David Ellison has announced a fresh masthead for the newly merged company.
fullText:
As Hollywood’s big five studios become the big three-and-a-half, CEO David Ellison has announced a fresh masthead for the newly merged company. Ignoring our many thoughtful suggestions (Warner’s Mount, Super Pario Bros. and Evil Wanker Inc. topped our internal poll), Skydance Media founder Ellison has named his new conglomerate, er, Skydance. “Paramount and Warner Bros. ... Warner Bros/Paramount to change name to Skydance

As Hollywood’s big five studios become the big three-and-a-half, CEO David Ellison has announced a fresh masthead for the newly merged company.

Ignoring our many thoughtful suggestions (Warner’s Mount, Super Pario Bros. and Evil Wanker Inc. topped our internal poll), Skydance Media founder Ellison has named his new conglomerate, er, Skydance.

“Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture”, the CEO posted to the social media platform growing like a fungus from Twitter’s code base earlier today, making ominous use of the past tense.

“By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history,” he continued, heading off accusations he’s planning some sort of Wikipedia find-and-replace heist. “We’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.”

It may be some time before audiences notice the change – Ellison has committed to keeping Warner Bros and Paramount distinct for the next five years, meaning the logo at the start of your next cinema trip probably won’t look very different (unless Skydance sneaks its own name in first). Once that five years is up, however? Just look again at that use of the past tense…

Between them, Skydance, Universal and Disney will control 75 per cent of the the US cinemagoing market, based on 2025 figures. With Sony covering just seven percent last year, the modern theatrical experience is almost completely dominated by these three companies.

The new company, which shares an only coincidental linguistic similarity to dystopian Terminator-providers Skynet, crossed its final regulatory hurdle when a judge approved the settlement between Ellison and a twelve-state coalition on Wednesday. Ellison and newly appointed co-CEO Ynon Kreiz now have the enviable task of managing the organisation’s roughly $80bn of combined debt and making $6bn in savings, presumably by firing a few people less important than they are.

title: CounterSteer: Suppressing Indirect Prompt Injection with Activation Steering
description: Indirect prompt injection makes an LLM agent treat untrusted retrieved text as instructions. We present CounterSteer, an inference-time defense that suppresses this behavior inside the model. Per model, a five-step recipe fits a residual-stream direction from paired episodes differing only in whether an embedded instruction is followed, and retains it only if it passes pre-specified causal and capability gates. At deployment, the direction is subtracted from every tool-result token during prefill. The edit is always on--there is no detection decision to evade--and requires no fine-tuning, auxiliary model, or added tokens, only white-box serving and tool-result span boundaries.

title: How the aggressive lone star tick unleashed a hidden meat allergy on millions of Americans
description:
Patrick Roden-Reynolds, a public health biologist, uses tweezers to remove ticks from a deer carcass in West Tisbury, a town on Martha's Vineyard, Mass. (Molly Peters / For The Times)
Like a matador swirling his cape, Patrick Roden-Reynolds pulled a swatch of white flannel this way and that on the grass and leaf litter in my yard. After a minute or so, he plucked 11 tiny ticks from the cloth with tweezers, and stuck them on a lint roller.
“It’s like a plague,” he said, peering at his haul. “Ticks are everywhere now.
fullText:
Like a matador swirling his cape, Patrick Roden-Reynolds pulled a swatch of white flannel this way and that on the grass and leaf litter in my yard. After a minute or so, he plucked 11 tiny ticks from the cloth with tweezers, and stuck them on a lint roller.

"It's like a plague," he said, peering at his haul. "Ticks are everywhere now."

I had asked Roden-Reynolds, a public health biologist, to inspect my yard because a lone star tick bit me as I was chopping wood last fall. It wasn't painful, but after several weeks I developed alpha-gal syndrome, an increasingly common allergy to red meat, dairy and other mammalian food products.

Like many on Martha's Vineyard, a resort island off Cape Cod that's teeming with ticks this year, I bid a sad farewell to hamburgers, bacon and lamb chops. No ice cream. No pizza. My medicine cabinet became a minefield of animal-derived byproducts, including gelatin capsules and pain meds with lactose.

If I err, and I do, my legs sometimes itch so fiercely they feel on fire and I break out in hives. I grew ill one night just from the fumes of grilling meat. And I've got a mild case. Some victims suffer headaches, nausea, fever, diarrhea, vomiting or abdominal cramps so sharp that a friend calls them "knives in the stomach."

Martha's Vineyard, long known for attracting celebrities, has become the inevitable butt of memes as it battles the hostile arachnids. Editors from London to Hollywood, elated that blood-sucking predators are attacking A-listers on their private beaches, have posted lurid headlines about "Vegan Vampire" ticks and "Billionaires Under Siege."

The mechanical chomping shark in "Jaws," which was filmed on the Vineyard in 1975, invariably gets a mention. As in the thriller, anxious local leaders debated whether publicizing the peril would scare off tourists.

The island's troubles are another reminder of the unexpected effects of climate change. Once confined to the Southeast, lone star ticks spread from Maine to Oklahoma in recent years as the climate warmed and as a decline in hunting led to an explosive growth in the number of whitetail deer, where lone stars find mates and breed.

The tick-borne allergy was discovered only in 2007, and researchers still can't say why some immune systems go haywire and some don't. A delayed reaction adds to the muddle because most victims don't get sick until hours after eating, and weeks or months after the tick bite. There's no known cure.

"It's enigmatic enough that it's almost the stuff of sci-fi or fantasy," said Dr. Jeffrey Wilson, a University of Virginia School of Medicine allergist and immunologist who has treated nearly 1,000 alpha-gal patients. Many were dumbfounded to discover that food they'd enjoyed all their lives suddenly made them deathly ill.

"For a lot of people, this is antithetical to being American," Wilson told me. "They say, 'I want to go outside and do what I want to do. I want to eat a hamburger.'"

At a party on the Vineyard recently, I met Jean-Marc Dupon, a 61-year-old former French chef who can no longer work in a professional kitchen due to his alpha-gal. He was twice rushed to the hospital after his throat closed, he couldn't breathe and his blood pressure plummeted — a severe allergic reaction called anaphylaxis.

He was so stricken when a local restaurant mistakenly grilled his food in butter, instead of oil, that he was unconscious when the ambulance arrived.

"It's not just an inconvenience for me," he said. "It's a matter of life and death."

The first alpha-gal fatality was confirmed in 2025 after Brian Waitzel, an otherwise healthy JetBlue pilot, died four hours after he ate a hamburger at a backyard barbecue in New Jersey. Experts say other deaths almost certainly have occurred.

It's unclear how many people are affected, but in July, a study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention concluded that an accurate tally would "far exceed" the CDC's 2022 estimate of 450,000 Americans.

That study found 1 in 4 adults tested positive for alpha-gal in the five worst-hit states — Arkansas, Kentucky, Missouri, Tennessee and Virginia, or more than 4 million people. The counting is tricky, however. Only a small percentage of those who test positive, perhaps 15%, show symptoms.

Those who do often struggle to get help. A 2017 study in North Carolina found more than 90% of alpha-gal cases were misdiagnosed, often as food poisoning, because doctors were unfamiliar with it. My dermatologist in Washington, D.C., didn't even know a blood test could measure alpha-gal antibodies.

Nancy Slonim Aronie, a writer and artist friend on the Vineyard, had a more alarming experience after she was rushed to a hospital in Boston in January for open heart surgery.

"The surgeon told me I might need a new heart valve, and that she had a cow valve she could use," Aronie recalled. "And I said, 'No, no, no, I have alpha-gal.' And she said, 'What's that?' And I thought, 'Wow, my surgeon doesn't know about alpha-gal.' And then she said, 'No problem, I think I have a pig valve on the shelf.'" And I'm like, 'No pig!'"

In the end, she didn't need a replacement valve. But she was treated with heparin, an anticoagulant derived from intestinal tissue of pigs. She broke out in hives, and "since then I've had really bad alpha-gal, much worse than before the operation."

Lone star ticks, named for the white dot on the female's back, haven't hit California. But the western blacklegged tick, known as the deer tick in most of the country, is common in the state's chaparral, grasslands and woods, and can transmit Lyme disease, babesiosis and other pathogens.

Luckily, those diseases can be cured by antibiotics or other remedies. Plus, an infected deer tick must keep its harpoon-like feeding tube in the bloodstream for 36 to 48 hours to transmit the bacteria that causes Lyme disease. That's enough time for many to remove the tick.

A lone star bite, in contrast, instantly injects a galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose carbohydrate molecule into the blood. The sugar, found in most mammals but not in humans, prompts the antibodies that trigger an allergic reaction.

Lone stars are tough little buggers. Though low temperatures will plunge them into dormancy, they produce a type of antifreeze that lets them survive harsh winters. They can stay hours underwater, and have no natural predators. And they've been around since the dinosaurs.

"It's the most aggressive tick in North America," said Thomas Mather, professor of public health entomology and head of a tick research center at the University of Rhode Island. It's also apparently the swiftest.

"If ESPN ever puts a tick race on TV, always put your money on the lone star," he said.

Sensory organs in their eight feet and two antenna-like palps sense heat or carbon dioxide from people passing by, and they quickly climb aboard, piercing the flesh with long, barbed mouthparts.

"Think of them as a cross between a lentil and a velociraptor," the National Society of Professional Surveyors, a group not normally known for purple prose, warns on its website. "These aggressive hunters," it adds, "will actively pursue you across significant distances."

On the Vineyard, local health officials call the threat a crisis. The Martha's Vineyard Hospital has tallied an exponential rise in positive alpha-gal tests — 692 this year through August, compared with 742 last year, and up from only two in 2020.

"It is the most pressing emerging illness on the island right now," Claire Seguin, president of the Martha's Vineyard Hospital, told me. "It seems everyone I know has, or knows someone who has, alpha-gal syndrome, including here at the hospital."

To ease pressure on the emergency room, the hospital opened a special outpatient clinic in June for tick-bite victims, and nearly 400 people were treated. The hospital also launched a $4-million research project into why only some people are affected and why their reactions vary so dramatically.

"Fear of tick bites rather than shark attacks now dominate the conversation," agreed an op-ed in the Vineyard Gazette. "Like lead in the water in Flint, Mich., and the forest fires out West, the very fabric of our lives is being altered."

"The situation is untenable," Virginia Barbatti, executive director of Tick Free MV, a new nonprofit group that is trying to coordinate a response, told me. "What's clear is everyone wants a path to solving this crisis."

In response, school lunch menus were revamped to offer more meatless and dairy-free options. Restaurants in the island's six towns, from the Sweet Life Cafe in Oak Bluffs to the Fish House in Edgartown, tweaked menus, recipes and how they cook.

"I switch out my pans, and I'm careful with knives and cutting boards to avoid cross contamination," said Charlie Granquist, chef at Slough Farm. "I just know so many people with alpha-gal."

He said his wife discovered her allergy only this spring when she "turned red as an Oompa Loompa" and went into anaphylaxis two hours after eating a hamburger.

At least nine companies sell pricey pesticide treatments or natural oil sprays for the backyard that are supposed to repel deer, or ticks, sparking an angry debate over whether they also endanger pets and pollinators. But other than avoiding tick bites, there's no obvious solution.

"The holy grail is a tick vaccine," Lea Hamner, an epidemiologist with a tick-focused program on the island, told an anxious crowd at one of the many public meetings focused on ticks. "People are working on it. But it's a long way off."

For now efforts are aimed at culling the vast deer herd. An aerial drone survey in March counted 4,681 white-tailed deer. It's now probably closer to 6,000, far more than the 1,500 deemed optimal for wildlife management and tick control.

Officials have considered mass sterilization or hiring sharpshooters, but those options are wildly expensive. A treatment to eliminate ticks on deer, like a tick collar on dogs, shows promise. A proposed Roomba-like device to suck ticks out of the grass probably does not.

Hoping to boost the deer harvest, Massachusetts extended the Vineyard's hunting season, which started Sept. 21, by six weeks, but most of the island's 183 registered hunters only kill one or two deer a year — hardly enough to make a major impact.

But Brian Athearn, 54, is determined to try. An avid bowhunter, he shot 42 deer last year and hopes to take more this year. He donates the venison to food pantries because he has alpha-gal and his son "almost died from anaphylactic shock from two Advil gel caps," he told me.

"I'm in it for revenge now," he said.

Athearn has gone vegan, but I'm not there yet. I enjoy eating emu and ostrich, which taste surprisingly like beef. We also get pork chops that were genetically modified to remove the alpha-gal molecule, the byproduct of efforts to produce safe pig-based substances for pharmaceuticals.

When I'm futzing in the garden or hiking, I wear socks, pants and shirts permeated with the tick-killing insecticide permethrin. As insurance, I tuck my shirt in, pull my socks over my pant legs, and wear ankle-covering gaiters. It's not high fashion, but I've avoided another bite. One friend wears her gaiters on the beach. I'm not there yet either.

On a recent afternoon I joined Roden-Reynolds, the public health biologist, as he surveyed an elderly couple's yard in Chilmark, a tick hot spot. We both suited up in permethrin-infused clothes and gaiters, and he went to work with his white flannel flag, dragging it to and fro on the grass.

"We've gone from zero to crisis in five years," he said as he stalked his prey.

He stopped after a few minutes to count his catch. "I'm just about getting a tick on every drag now," he said. "There's 11, 12, 13."

He started up again but wiped his brow and quit when he hit 37.

Drogin is a special correspondent.

A. Times and beyond in your inbox six days a week.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.

title: Most MLB postseason home runs: See the all-time list of career leaders
description: These MLB sluggers have the most home runs in postseason history.
fullText:
Major League Baseball's further-expanded postseason probably means that no playoff records will be safe in the years to come, with more October games than ever before.

All 18 of Mickey Mantle's home runs came in the World Series as the Hall of Famer retired before the introduction of the League Championship Series in 1969. Previously, the top team in each league would go directly to the World Series at the end of the regular season.

These days with a 12-team postseason field, a team can play up to 22 games – compared to seven in Mantle's day – meaning plenty more opportunities to accumulate stats on baseball's biggest stage.

But Manny Ramirez, who last played in the postseason in 2009, still holds the record with 29 home runs in the postseason. Jose Altuve ranks second in history with 28 – including one in the AL wild card series – but the Houston Astros will have to get back to the postseason

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo Guarantees Miami Heat Title Win
description: The Miami Heat has a lot of pressure on them to contend for NBA Championship wins every season moving forward. Trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo made the team’s timeline change with a superstar and fewer younger players on the roster. Miami also added veterans Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway to complete the roster with established winning […] The post Giannis Antetokounmpo Guarantees Miami Heat Title Win appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Miami Heat has a lot of pressure on them to contend for NBA Championship wins every season moving forward. Trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo made the team's timeline change with a superstar and fewer younger players on the roster. Miami also added veterans Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway to complete the roster with established winning players. Antetokounmpo played his first preseason game with the Heat to show off his look in the new uniform.

However, the biggest takeaway came from Giannis' comments guaranteeing an NBA Championship win:

"It starts today, but I've realized, like, not to put a lot of pressure on myself and the team. It's going to happen. It's going to take time. Like, we're preparing for something that will take place in June, and it's September. You know, like, it's going to take time.

But we are—I know, like, the people that I have next to me have the same mindset. Bam (Adebayo) wants to win. Coach wants to win. The organization, they want to win. So, but slowly, slowly, we're going to be at the place that we're supposed to be."

Antetokounmpo added that it's going to take time to become a great team but that a title win "is going to happen" with him on the roster. Pat Riley traded Tyler Herro and a handful of other young assets to bring in a two-time MVP winner. The goal is clearly to win at least one NBA Championship in the Giannis era, and he fully believes it will happen.

It is important to note that Antetokounmpo did not say which season the NBA Championship is going to happen. Miami is considered a secondary contender this season behind more complete rosters like the New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers.

However, the long season will give the Heat plenty of time to develop chemistry and see how the players fit together. Role players like Andrew Wiggins and Davion Mitchell will need to have great seasons for Miami to make up the gap with better teams.

Giannis' health remains the most important factor since history shows he's good enough to lead a team to regular season success when healthy. The Milwaukee Bucks have been a great regular season team every year in recent memory until Antetokounmpo's injury ruined them last season.

The star power at the top is always pivotal for any title contending teams. Jalen Brunson and Jayson Tatum give their respective top East teams a huge advantage by contributing All-NBA level basketball almost every single night.

Giannis must do that for Miami by staying healthy and going back to the form he was at in Milwaukee before injuries slowed him down. Another injury riddled season could add fear over Antetokounmpo ever being able to lead a team to the championship again.

Head coach Erik Spolestra believes in the team dynamic making them a viable contender as soon as this season. It all starts with Giannis, and he is buying into the vision of Spo and the Heat roster moving forward.

title: Blake Snell leaves Dodgers in difficult position vs Braves
description: Blake Snell doesn't even make it through 4 innings Sunday night.
fullText:
Blake Snell put the Los Angeles Dodgers in a difficult position during their MLB playoff game. Snell started Game 2 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves and exited after just 3.2 innings and 90 pitches.

Blake Snell is coming out after 3.2 innings at 90 pitches https://t.co/nKXliDyA5w

— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 5, 2026

While Snell allowed only one earned run, the high pitch count forced the Dodgers to ask their bullpen to cover more than five innings in a crucial playoff game.

MORE: Every MLB team's most recent playoff win: Which franchise has the longest drought?

Nov 1, 2025; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell (7) throws pitch against the Toronto Blue Jays in the eighth inning for game seven of the 2025 MLB World Series at Rogers Centre. Mandatory Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images

Snell's final line was respectable from a run-prevention standpoint, but the efficiency simply was not there. He allowed three hits and one earned run while striking out five, but he also walked five batters and needed 90 pitches to record only 11 outs.

That combination is particularly problematic in October. Starting pitchers are expected to provide length whenever possible because playoff bullpens can quickly become exhausted when multiple relievers are required to cover significant innings.

Snell had returned from an elbow issue earlier in the season and is expected to be relied upon heavily in the playoffs.

Aug 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell (7) completes another inning at the top of the seventh inning agains the Pittsburgh Pirates at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The biggest concern for Los Angeles is what Snell's early exit means for the rest of the game. Asking the bullpen to record more than 15 outs against an Atlanta lineup in a playoff game is a difficult task, particularly with the Dodgers already managing their pitching staff carefully throughout October.

The Dodgers opened the NLDS with Tarik Skubal throwing six innings in Game 1, giving the bullpen a much-needed break.

But Snell's inability to get through even four innings creates a completely different situation in Game 2.

Allowing one earned run over 3.2 innings is not a disastrous performance on its own. However, needing 90 pitches to get there means Snell did not give the Dodgers the length they needed from one of their premier starters.

In a best-of-five playoff series, every bullpen inning matters. Snell's lack of efficiency could ultimately force Los Angeles to lean heavily on its relievers and potentially impact the team's pitching plans for the remainder of the series.

title: ‘I’ll Always Take the Blame,’ ‘I Don’t Have No Comment’ — Todd Bowles’ Job Security in Question as Buccaneers Drop to 0-4
description: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 17-14 home loss to the Green Bay Packers in undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels’ first NFL start, and coach Todd Bowles said the blame belonged to his team. “It’s on us,” Bowles said.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 17-14 home loss to the Green Bay Packers in undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels' first NFL start, and coach Todd Bowles said the blame belonged to his team.

"It's on us," Bowles said. "We know what the problem is. It's on us. We can't keep getting close and not winning. That's not good enough."

Tampa Bay lost its first three games 33-27 at Cincinnati, 23-19 to Cleveland and 23-16 to Minnesota, making Sunday its fourth straight loss by seven points or fewer. The Buccaneers are 0-4 for the first time since 2013, according to the team.

Some fans called for Bowles to go, and two-time All-Pro tackle Tristan Wirfs declined to comment when asked about his coach's job security.

"I don't have no comment," Wirfs said when asked what he would tell ownership in Bowles' defense. "I love coach Bowles, yeah, I don't know."

Wirfs put the burden on the players. "No one is coming to save us," he said. "We aren't going to magically get a superhero in here." He added, "It's the guys in this locker room that are going to get us out of it."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Pewter Report, which covers the Buccaneers, posted video of Wirfs' answer and described it as his reaction to "a question about Todd Bowles' job security."

Bowles took the blame himself. "I'm the head coach," he said. "I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame." He also said the team would stay together. "We're gonna fight, we're gonna stick together and we're gonna figure this thing out," Bowles added. "And I'll lead them to that. It's my job."

The Buccaneers marked the end of the game with a one-word post, "Final." "Embarrassing clean house," one fan replied. "It's time for Bowles to retire," another wrote.

Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and he ran eight times for 55 yards. Green Bay turned the interceptions into 10 points, including Trey Smack's 58-yard field goal as the first half ended.

Jordan Love threw 2-yard touchdown passes to Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft, and the Packers led 17-7 until Daniels hit Kenny Gainwell for a 10-yard score early in the fourth quarter. Tampa Bay's defense then forced two turnovers, a fumble recovered by Zyon McCollum at the Buccaneers' 4 and a Jacob Parrish interception at the 7, but neither led to points.

The last drive reached the Green Bay 46 before safety Evan Williams came in unblocked on fourth-and-11 and Daniels' throw fell incomplete with 1:25 left. Daniels took responsibility for the protection. "If I flip that and make sure that we're able to slide to him, he doesn't get free and I'm able to make a throw," he said.

Before that play, Bowles passed on what would have been a 65-yard field-goal attempt by Chase McLaughlin, whose career long of 65 yards came last season. "It was too far for us, a good 10 to 15 yards too far for us," Bowles said. "The wind was blowing that way as well. We thought about it, didn't feel good about it."

One fan asked "why not give Chase a chance to kick it" and took aim at Bowles and offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. "I can't wait to pay for Bowles and Zac Robinson Uber to Tampa International Airport," the fan wrote, adding that the "Defense & Special Teams played good enough and Offense line failed the test again."

Daniels was sacked three times, and Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks in four games. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards and was not sacked.

Another fan took a sarcastic shot at the timeout Tampa Bay called just before Smack's kick. "The Bucs are 0-4, we love Todd Bowles for icing the kicker at the half, those 3 points lost them the game," the fan wrote.

The loss was Tampa Bay's 11th in its last 13 games dating to last season, when the Bucs opened 6-2 before losing seven of their final nine to miss the playoffs. The Buccaneers had won four division titles and a Super Bowl in the previous six seasons. Bowles is under contract through 2028, according to The Associated Press.

Pewter Report noted that Bowles "will not speak on the team's extended struggles going back to last year, but he did speak on starting the year 0-4."

Only one team in NFL history, the 1992 San Diego Chargers, has made the playoffs after an 0-4 start, according to the team. Bowles kept his focus on the next game. "We're just trying to get a win against the Cowboys, then we'll go from there," he said.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

One fan responded to FOX Sports NFL writer Greg Auman's video of Bowles' postgame remarks. "He can say that all day, and he does," the fan wrote. "But nothing is happening to change it. It's all talk." He added, "It's been time for a change since January of 2025."

Daniels will start again Thursday. "Yeah, he'll be the quarterback Thursday night," Bowles said. "He had some ups and he had some downs, but for his first time out there, he didn't panic, he didn't do anything. He escaped, used his legs well at times."

Baker Mayfield, who had started 57 consecutive games for Tampa Bay including the postseason, dislocated his right thumb late in the Week 3 loss to Minnesota and is expected to miss at least two more games.

The Buccaneers visit the Dallas Cowboys (2-2) on Thursday night. Dallas beat Houston 34-30 on Sunday.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Tetairoa McMillan's second TD catch gives Panthers 22-16 lead over Lions
description: Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was limited to just two catches for 17 yards in last week’s loss to Cleveland.
fullText:
Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan was limited to just two catches for 17 yards in last week's loss to Cleveland.

Apparently, he took that personally.

McMillan caught his second touchdown of the night to cap Carolina's opening possession of the third quarter, giving the Panthers a 22-16 lead over the Lions.

After catching a 32-yard TD earlier, McMillan's second scoring strike was for 10 yards.

But that gave him 11 catches for 162 yards on the night.

McMillan entered Week 4 with 12 catches for 193 yards with no TDs.

He's already blown past his previous career highs in receptions (eight) and yards (130).

We'll see what he can do for the rest of the game.

title: ‘Nobody in the National Media Cares’ — Life Surge Claps Back at Pablo Torre for Targeting Tim Tebow ‘to Draw a Million Podcast Views’
description: The gloves are off as Life Surge pushes back on Pablo Torre’s investigation. The Christian events company says Tim Tebow’s fame helped turn scrutiny of its business into a national story.
fullText:
The gloves are off as Life Surge pushes back on Pablo Torre's investigation.

The Christian events company says Tim Tebow's fame helped turn scrutiny of its business into a national story. Its latest statement took a swipe at Torre's podcast audience while defending the former Florida quarterback, who has paused his relationship with the company.

"Life Surge is not big enough to draw a million podcast views on its own. Nobody in the national media cares that much about a one-day event in Columbus or Atlanta," the company said in astatement Torre shared.

The company accused the coverage of leaning on Tebow's reputation to get attention.

"So, this story was packaged around the most trusted Christian voice in American sports, and Tim Tebow's name is what made it travel,"Life Surge continued.

That puts Torre's motives squarely in the company's crosshairs. Life Surge's position is that the attention followed Tebow's name, and it believes the coverage unfairly made him the centerpiece.

Torre and Mother Jones reporter Kiera Butler published their investigation on Sept. 24. Their reporting examined allegations that Life Surge used attendees' faith and aggressive sales tactics to steer them toward expensive financial education programs.

DIVE IN: PFN's Free CFB HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More

The company disputed those characterizations in an earlier response published by Torre. It said enrollment in its $97 Impact Classes and advanced training was voluntary, and that it did not train representatives to push customers into debt they could not afford.

Life Surge also said it did not ask headline speakers to endorse those programs. Torre published the company's detailed response alongside the episode and said he stood by the reporting.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Tebow had alreadypaused his relationship with Life Surge and announced that his team would investigate. On Sept. 25, he called the allegations "extremely, extremely serious."

The company's new statement expressed support for him.

"We love Tim. He has stood on our stages for years, his compensation has never been tied to the sale of anything, and what he brings to a crowd is a call to serve Jesus and to serve others,"Life Surge said.

"He has chosen to pause with Life Surge while his team gets to the facts, and we understand."

That compensation claim matters to Life Surge's defense of Tebow. The company is saying his speaking work carried no financial incentive tied to customers buying its products.

For Tebow, the uncomfortable part is already clear. Life Surge is defending his reputation publicly while he takes a closer look at the company behind the stages he stood on. His next decision will say plenty about whether that relationship has a future.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: What is the Eagles’ offensive identity? Not ‘good enough,’ says Nick Sirianni after loss to Rams | The Early Bird
description: Eagles fans flocked to the exits as Jalen Hurts commanded the huddle on the Eagles’ final drive. The offense faced third-and-17 with the game on the line, but the result...
fullText:
Eagles fans flocked to the exits as Jalen Hurts commanded the huddle on the Eagles' final drive.

The offense faced third-and-17 with the game on the line, but the result felt like a foregone conclusion.

The Eagles lost, 24-20, to the Los Angeles Rams and fell to 2-2. The offense turned in a listless second half, the defense capitulated two back-breaking drives late, and somehow this team erased a 10-point lead built up mostly off turnovers and some opportune moments from reserve wide receiver Darius Cooper in the end zone.

Afterward, Hurts summed the afternoon up with two words, over and over.

The Eagles finishing 0-for-12 on third down in the game, the worst ratio from any Eagles game since 1991?

What about the Eagles once-again stagnant offense in third quarter? The offense has managed just three first downs in the third quarter across all four of the games they've played this season, the worst tally in the NFL by a wide margin. The group has just 12 second-half first downs, which is also the worst total in the league.

Hurts finished the game 12-for-27 for just 93 passing yards and two touchdowns set up by takeaways on defense. Beside two games that he left due to injury, Sunday was the lowest yardage tally Hurts has recorded since becoming the Eagles starting quarterback in 2021.

This is as good a time as any to contextualize the offensive performance. The group came into the game without DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, or Lane Johnson. Johnson was a late addition to the inactives list for personal reasons. Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter with a hamstring injury and did not return as well.

Players did not know Johnson would be unavailable until they reported to the stadium the morning of the game, Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni did not offer any details about Johnson's absence, either. Missing the 36-year-old gave way to the Eagles starting third-round rookie Markel Bell at right tackle without another healthy tackle on the active roster. It also left them with just seven offensive linemen available to dress, meaning the team was one player short of the permitted 48 on the active roster because that number requires at least eight offensive linemen to be included.

"I've got to figure it out," Hurts said when asked about the injuries. "However it looks, whatever it means. Find a way to win the game."

Most importantly, the late switch left the Eagles offense seemingly even less prepared for the pressure wrinkles from the Rams. According to Next Gen Stats, Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula sent extra rushers at Hurts on 18 of his dropbacks (60.6%), with Hurts going 5-for-16 on those plays. And on the Eagles' 12 third downs, the Rams blitzed on all but one.

When asked about those issues, Hurts defaulted back to the line of the day.

"Poor execution," Hurts said. "I don't think there's any other way to put it."

The optimist's view of the Eagles' second-half collapse will likely point to the absence of quite possibly the four most important offensive contributors not named Jalen Hurts for most of the game. The team entered Sunday as underdogs and perhaps wouldn't have been viewed as harshly if not for a somewhat overachieving first-half performance relative to what most expected the game to look like because of the injury report.

Still, facing third-and-goal from the two-yard line with a 10-point lead and 8 minutes remaining, the Eagles somehow managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory largely due to an offense devoid of an identity.

"Right now, it hasn't been good enough," Sirianni said. "I think that's still. You're trying to make sure as you find out who you are that you're playing with detail and you're playing with together and you're playing with toughness. We've still got ways to go there. It's obvious that we're still trying to figure that out."

The detail, in particular, has been lacking. A botched play came on the pivotal third-and-goal, courtesy of Cam Jurgens pulling across the formation and interfering with Hurts trying to secure the snap and hand the bal off to Tank Bigsby. And facing fourth-and-goal from the 2, Sirianni elected to keep the offense on the field for an incomplete pass to Cooper.

Sirianni was (understandably) aggressive trying to make it a three-possession game, but the decision backfired. The Rams drove 98 yards for a touchdown and got the ball back quickly after the Eagles offense turned in its 19th three-and-out of the season (second highest in the NFL.)

"I'm trying to make it a three-score game," Sirianni said. "We would have went up 13, but I wanted to make it a three-score game right there. Fourth-and-2 from the 2, you leave them in a true backed-up scenario. I'm very well aware of how fourth-down decisions go as the head coach. You go for it and you get it, great. You go for it and you don't get it, that's on the head coach. And we didn't get it, so that's on me."

An optimist's view would also point to the fact that the Eagles have been here before with Hurts under center and Sirianni at the helm. You might remember the team also got off to a 2-2 start in 2024. The offensive line implored Sirianni to pivot toward more of a run-first approach, Sirianni shaved his head, and the Eagles went on a magical run to Super Bowl LIX and left Caesars Superdome with the organization's second Lombardi Trophy.

That page doesn't seem to be in Sean Mannion's 2026 playbook, though. The Eagles ranked fifth in EPA/rush through the first four games of 2024. This season, they're 24th. They've had moving pieces along the offensive line in three of the first four games and Barkley has now suffered a stinger and a hamstring injury already this season. Backup running back Tank Bigsby also suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter.

What is apparent is that the Eagles now have an urgency to figure out what this year's about face is going to look like. A training camp spent harping on under-center formations and play-action passing concepts hasn't kept them from ranking in the bottom five in the NFL in terms of usage in both categories.

Less than a week removed from challenging his teammates to ask themselves "who are we?" in the wake of the loss to the Bears, Hurts didn't have much of an answer himself to explain the second defeat in a six-day span.

"You're finding your flow," Hurts said. "I think collectively as a unit, it comes down to finding your flow and finding your rhythm as a unit and going out there and executing at a high level. We didn't do that."

title: Report: Chiefs are "very interested" in a Tyreek Hill reunion
description: Last year, before then-Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a serious knee injury, the Chiefs were interested in trading for him.
fullText:
Last year, before then-Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a serious knee injury, the Chiefs were interested in trading for him. Now that he's available to be signed by anyone, the Chiefs are interested in signing him.

Via Mike Silver of The Athletic, the Chiefs are "very interested" in a reunion with Hill. The team, per Silver, has already reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, regarding the possibility of bringing Hill back.

The first question is Hill's health. Silver says he's targeting a return in November.

Hill posted "hm" on Twitter after Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. Receiver Rashee Rice injured a hamstring earlier in the game.

A fifth-round pick in 2016, the 32-year-old Hill spent six seasons in Kansas City. A big contract for receiver Davante Adams in March 2022 prompted Hill to seek a trade to a team that would pay him more.

He spent four years with the Dolphins.

As Silver explains, multiple Chiefs players endorsed Hill's potential return.

"That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," tight end Travis Kelce said. "He's a brother. He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."

"I have no idea [if that would happen], but it'd be pretty cool," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said.

Defensive tackle Chris Jones was more blunt: "I hope we do. It'd be dangerous. . . . Dangerous!"

During a media tour in New Orleans prior to Super Bowl LIX, Hill admitted that he regrets leaving the Chiefs. If/when he's healthy, he could get a chance to return — fueling the effort to chase another Super Bowl ring.

title: Utah Mammoth lose their 1st game of the season
description: Rangers forward Will Cuylle laid a dangerous hit on Mammoth star Dylan Guenther on Sunday. Here’s why it’s so serious.
fullText:
For the first time ever, the Utah Mammoth have lost a game in the state of New York.

The team went 6-0-0 there in their first two seasons, beating the New York Rangers, New York Islanders and Buffalo Sabres every time they headed east. Ironically, that changed as soon as the Mammoth acquired star forwards from both the Rangers and the Islanders.

Sunday's visit to Madison Square Garden proved to be the Mammoth's first true test of the 2026-27 season. After missing the playoffs the last two seasons, the Rangers seem intent on changing their fortune — and they've looked like a team to beat thus far.

"I thought the effort was there. We worked hard, we competed, we battled," said Andrew Peeke, who scored his first goal as a Mammoth in the game. "... Just a little sloppy on some execution things. We made (goaltender Karel Vejmelka) have to stand on his head."

The Mammoth's problem came from odd-man rushes. They allowed two breakaways in the first period, plus a 3-on-0, a 3-on-1 and a handful of 2-on-1s throughout the game. Vejmelka bailed his team out on most of them, but he could only do so much.

GABE WITH THE REBOUND 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/eOh9epZNCn

Head coach André Tourigny gave his diagnosis after the game.

"We were impatient. We were forcing plays. Instead of reloading quickly and being above (the puck), we were forcing things. We were waiting to see if we would cut the play before we reloaded. (In this) league, there's no forgiveness," he said.

"Don't get me wrong: Our reloads is one of our strengths. ... If we don't reload properly, that will cost us."

In December 2011, Jack Jablonski, a high school hockey player in Minnesota, crashed head-first into the boards after taking a hit from behind, and it left him a quadriplegic.

That situation is not unique to Jablonski — it's a real danger in the game of hockey — which is why "boarding" is such a serious penalty.

Mammoth forward Dylan Guenther was on the receiving end of a similar hit Sunday, though he was fortunate to avoid Jablonski's outcome. Guenther had a split second to turn his body, giving his shoulder the brunt of the impact rather than his head.

The rulebook states that the onus is on the offending player to avoid the hit if his opponent is in a vulnerable position. However, it also lists several potential mitigating factors for the referees to consider when making the call:

The degree of the impact with the boards.

Whether it results in an injury to the face or the head.

Whether the check could have been avoided.

Whether the opponent put himself in a vulnerable position immediately before or during the check.

In this instance, Rangers forward Will Cuylle, who threw the hit, was not forced into a corner. He was not off-balance. He could have eased up on the hit. He chose not to, and instead risked the long-term health of another person.

Despite all that, Cuylle got nothing more than a slap on the wrist in the form of a minor penalty.

I don't care about the implications on the game, but I do care about the safety of the players.

This was a dirty hit that has no place in hockey. The fact that this was only a 2-minute minor is an absolute joke.#TusksUp #NYR https://t.co/sxcnbFCLAl

The applicable mitigating factors in this instance were that Guenther did not sustain an injury and that he was slightly crouched when Cuylle initiated the hit.

Jack McBain, who roomed with Guenther the past two seasons, stood up for his teammate at his first opportunity, dropping the gloves. Cuylle is no stranger to fighting and held his own in the scrap.

Cuylle brushed it off after the game.

"Obviously they thought it was a dirty hit, so, I guess, just answer the bell," he said. "They challenged me, so (I had to) just stand up for myself. They've got to stand up for their guys. That's hockey. Happy to do it."

title: Tobias Harris could miss Spurs season opener after straining calf
description: Tobias Harris suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the NBA preseason, the San Antonio Spurs announced.
fullText:
Newly acquired free agent Tobias Harris will be questionable for the San Antonio Spurs' Oct. 20 season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Harris suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will miss the NBA preseason. The Spurs announced the news before their intrasquad scrimmage on Sunday, Oct. 4.

Harris did not play in the scrimmage as a result of the injury and the team said he will be evaluated after the preseason.

In July, the 34-year-old forward signed a two-year, $31 million deal to join the Spurs, who reached the NBA Finals in 2026 before losing to the New York Knicks in five games.

He spent the past two seasons with the Detroit Pistons and served as a veteran presence on one of the NBA's youngest rosters. The 15-year NBA veteran also played for the Pistons earlier in his career.

Harris previously played more than five years for the Philadelphia 76ers and had stints with the Los Angeles Clippers, Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks

Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists for Detroit in 63 games played last season and helped the Pistons earn the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference before they were eliminated by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the conference semifinals in seven games.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Tobias Harris could miss Spurs season opener after straining calf

title: Austin Cindric feels like he’s right on the edge of winning
description: Austin Cindric has had two of his strongest finishes of the year the past two weeks, and believes he’s close to breaking through for a win
fullText:
Austin Cindric had another strong finish at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Sunday, taking fourth place in the South Point 400 to secure his second straight top-five of the Chase.

While Cindric was in the hunt for much of the race, it was Chase Briscoe who took the checkered flag with Kyle Larson and Tyler Reddick the most threatening cars to take the win from him in the late laps.

Still, Cindric believes he is right on the cusp of securing a win, and given how the No. 2 team looked both this week and last, there's good reason to believe him.

"I feel like we had a car that was pretty good, and close to capable of winning today," Cindric said. "A lot of déjà vu from last week with the leaders fighting for the win, still giving us the shot there. Just proud of everybody on the No. 2 car, to be able to bring two really fast cars two weeks in a row and really start to execute really well throughout this stretch."

Cindric credited his team for improving over the weekend, as the No. 2 was seventh in qualifying but wound up leading the race for 33 laps, more than any driver other than Briscoe or Denny Hamlin.

"It wasn't an easy weekend. We didn't start the race necessarily as close as we needed to. We didn't start practice necessarily as close as we needed to. Guys worked on it all day, gave us some strengths that we didn't have before. It takes a great team. That's what it takes to be good at this level on a consistent basis. Just want to win."

It feels like Cindric is right there, and he'll get another chance to compete for a win next week as the Chase heads to Charlotte. While Cindric is 128 points off of the Chase lead and almost assuredly out of the title race, he's clearly doing his best racing at the right time of the year, and seems ready to turn one of his "so close" days into a victory.

title: Mason Miller's uncharacteristic 9th-inning struggles put Padres on the verge of playoff elimination
description: — Mason Miller's emergence as the best closer in the major leagues helped get San Diego into the playoffs.His uncharacteristic troubles in the ninth inning Sunday have the Padres on the brink of elimination.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — Mason Miller's emergence as the best closer in the major leagues helped get San Diego into the playoffs.

His uncharacteristic troubles in the ninth inning Sunday have the Padres on the brink of elimination.

The two-time All-Star closer struggled with control, loading the bases in the ninth inning against Milwaukee with the first three walks of his postseason career as he tried to complete a six-out save.

Jackson Chourio followed with a walk-off, two-run single with two outs that dealt the Padres a 4-3 loss. San Diego went home in a 2-0 NL Division Series deficit heading into Game 3 Tuesday.

"I didn't do my job today, so instead of being here with a win and a series tie, we're in a hole," Miller said.

Miller's unsuccessful attempt at his first six-out save since 2024 came one day after Adrian Morejon gave up a tiebreaking homer to William Contreras in the seventh inning of a 3-2 defeat.

"Two really good games that didn't go our way," first baseman Ty France said. "Just go back home and play each game like it's our last."

San Diego's inability to protect two-run leads in each of these first two games is a notable turn of events for a team that could shorten games much of the season because of its deep corps of relief pitchers.

The hard-throwing Miller led the bullpen brigade by collecting 38 saves and posting a 1.67 ERA while striking out 129 batters over 70 innings in the regular season. He threw 34 2/3 straight scoreless innings at one point in the season.

Miller hadn't been as dominant lately. He had an 0.79 ERA at the end of July before posting a 3.33 ERA from Aug. 1 through the end of the regular season. Even so, Miller's presence has given the Padres a sense of security they can maintain any late-inning lead.

Miller retired the side in order with a pair of strikeouts in the eighth inning and got the leadoff batter in the ninth with San Diego ahead 3-2.

That's when the problems started.

Christian Yelich walked on five pitches and stole second. Sal Frelick walked on a 3-2 pitch. After Miller retired Andrew Vaughn on a fly to center, Gary Sánchez walked while taking six straight pitches.

Chourio fell behind 1-2 in the count, fouled off Miller's fasted pitch of the day at 103.5 mph, then took a low slider before lining a 101.3 mph offering just past past second baseman Jake Cronenworth's attempt for a diving backhand stop and went into center field.

Although Miller threw 40 pitches — his most since 2023 — he said that didn't impact him and that he had felt fine. He topped 100 mph with 18 pitches.

"It's not the first save I've blown and it probably won't be the last one I blow, either," Miller said. "It's part of the job. Failure in my role is really hard to move past, I guess, when you look at it, because most of the time, when you fail, you lose. Other spots, you get another chance. That's part of it. I'm going to come back and be prepared to pitch Tuesday and do my best to help the team win."

San Diego remains confident it came rebound, If the Padres do, Miller likely would play a major role.

"He's been unbelievable ever since he put on a Padre uniform," pitcher Michael King said. "I know everybody in this locker room wants him with the ball in a big situation — and still does."

title: Sean Payton comments on Broncos' 3 notable injuries after loss
description: Broncos coach Sean Payton didn't have much of an update on Pat Surtain, Riley Moss and Pat Bryant following Sunday's loss.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos were hit hard by injuries during a 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.

Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) both went down in the first half, and wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle) was carted off the field in the third quarter. Denver coach Sean Payton did not have an immediate update on the three players during his post-game press conference.

"Well, I'm not going to give you any report on the injuries because I don't know [an update]," Payton said. "I would say it probably impacts the defense when both your corners are down coming into the second half, and then with Pat [Bryant]. So, nothing right now [to report]. I mean, I just asked the same question coming off the field to (VP of Player Health and Performance) Beau [Lowery]."

Payton is scheduled to have a conference call with reporters on Monday morning, and there might be more news on the statuses of Surtain, Moss and Bryant then. When asked specifically about Bryant after the game, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said he knows the receiver will be "aggressive in rehab." Whether that's a bad early sign for Bryant's status or merely a boilerplate response. More updates should arrive within the next 48 hours.

title: Philadelphia Eagles' Offense Sputters in Week 4 Loss to Rams
description: The Philadelphia Eagles' offense struggled in Week 4 in their loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Eagles dropped to 2-2 with a 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. It was a rough game for the Eagles, particularly on the offensive side of the ball.

Philadelphia entered the game without star wide receiver DeVonta Smith and right tackle Lane Johnson, which made it tough for the offense. The injury news didn't get any better for the Eagles, as star running back Saquon Barkley left with a hamstring injury in the first quarter.

Tank Bigsby stepped up as the lead back for Philadelphia, rushing for 55 yards on 14 carries. However, it wasn't a strong performance overall, as the Eagles rushed for 104 yards on 27 carries as a team and didn't find the end zone.

The passing attack wasn't much better, as Jalen Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 98 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Darius Cooper was the leading receiver for Philadelphia with three receptions for 33 yards and two touchdowns. Although Cooper showed flashes of his talent, it was overall a terrible display from the offense.

While the offense struggled mightily, the Eagles' defense played at a high level. Cooper DeJean and Andrew Mukuba both picked off Matthew Stafford and held the Rams' elite offense to 10 points through the first three quarters.

However, with the offense struggling to get on the scoreboard, Philadelphia's defense couldn't hold strong forever. In the fourth quarter, Stafford led a 10-play, 97-yard drive that culminated in a one-yard touchdown run by Kyren Williams, which cut the Eagles' lead to 20-17.

After a three-and-out by the Eagles offense, Los Angeles got the ball back and took full advantage. Stafford led a 10-play, 79-yard drive, with Williams punching it into the end zone on a seven-yard run. That gave the Rams a 24-20 lead with 1:10 left in the game.

Philadelphia had a chance to take the lead, but it went nowhere. Byron Young sacked Hurts on first down, which wasted a ton of time as the Eagles were without timeouts.

On 2nd-and-17, Hurts threw an incompletion intended for Cooper. Young sacked Hurts again on third down, setting up a desperation fourth-down pass that fell incomplete.

The Eagles offense has looked atrocious through the first four games of the season, despite winning two. While they have injuries to key players, Philadelphia's issues go beyond that, and first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion needs to get the unit on track in Week 5 against a talented Jacksonville Jaguars team.

title: Down to their last strike, Jackson Chourio and the Brewers find a way in NLDS Game 2: 'One of my favorite games I’ve been a part of'
description: The fans in Milwaukee didn't have a whole lot to cheer about for 8 2/3 innings. Then Chourio delivered.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE — More than 41,000 Brewers fans had little to celebrate going into the ninth inning of Game 2 of the NLDS on Sunday. As a matter of fact, they were probably frustrated most of the game. For eight innings, their Brewers had looked unrecognizable. Eight innings of sloppy baseball, including three errors and two unearned runs, combined with a lack of offense had the Brewers on the brink of losing their first game of this postseason to the San Diego Padres. And against MLB's best and most intimidating closer, Mason Miller, things looked grim.

Then the Brewers remembered who they are. It might've taken 8 2/3 innings, but in their 4-3 walkoff victory over the Padres in Game 2, they gave a sellout crowd at American Family Field a reason to cheer and a game they'll never forget.

"One of my favorite games I've been a part of," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "And what's most gratifying to see is how many of our great fans came out to see that one. Just happy for the club, happy for the city that they got to witness something so special."

But let's back up. Before Milwaukee could attempt to walk off the Padres, they first had to tie the game against Miller after entering the ninth down 3-2. And that required baserunners. Up to that point, San Diego had allowed very little traffic, and the Brewers had mustered just four hits prior to the ninth. But with the Brewers down to their final three outs, newly minted captain Christian Yelich worked a five-pitch walk against Miller to put the tying run on first base with one out.

Of course, one at-bat alone doesn't make for a comeback against the game's best reliever. But for a team like the Brewers, who have always believed as an organization that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts, the mindset was to keep the line moving.

"Just grind, man. Just find a way to get on there," Yelich said afterward. "Doesn't matter if it's a walk or a hit. We just want some traffic in that inning there, and just see what happens."

After drawing that walk, Yelich handed the baton to Sal Frelick. Frelick fell behind in the count 1-2 against Miller, a place no hitter wants to be. But then the Brewers' right fielder buckled down, taking three straight Miller pitches to draw another walk.

"Guys like that don't give up multiple hits in innings very often," Frelick said. "He was tasked with six outs today, so wanted to kind of get pressure on him, see if we could get some guys on."

Following an Andrew Vaughn flyout for the second out, arguably the biggest at-bat of the ninth came from catcher Gary Sánchez, who pinch hit for David Hamilton. Sánchez is on the Brewers' NLDS roster for moments like this — opportunities for a big swing. But just like his teammates, the veteran wasn't necessarily looking for a three-run shot.

Like Yelich and Frelick before him, Sánchez was able to grind and put together another tough at-bat against Miller. After working the count full, he drew the Brewers' third walk of the inning.

"He's the best in the game," first baseman Jake Bauers said of Miller before the series. "I think the mentality is try to have a good at-bat. Whatever happens after that is whatever happens."

Jackson Chourio's moment. #NoTimeLikeOctober pic.twitter.com/7yJ4ttQaqj

What happened is Milwaukee's biggest star came up in the biggest moment. With the bases loaded and two out in the bottom of the ninth, who else would step into the box but Jackson Chourio?

Having announced his presence in this series with a game-tying, two-run shot in the Brewers' Game 1 victory, Chourio had plenty of confidence going into his at-bat against Miller. And the 22-year-old wasn't trying to play here. He understood exactly what was unfolding.

"Watching those at-bats beforehand, I knew that he was a little bit erratic," Chourio said of Miller. "He was throwing some balls. I knew that he was gonna come at me with the fastball at some point, so mentally, I was just making sure that I was prepared for that."

The first two times Miller came at Chourio with the fastball, it worked; Chourio swung-and-missed at 100.8 mph and 102.2 mph before fouling off 103.5 mph. But after taking a tough slider to make it a 2-2 count, Chourio decided to call game.

Miller offered a 101.3 mph fastball, and Chourio ripped a 109.5 mph single into center field, past a diving Jake Cronenworth. Yelich scored easily from third, and as a flying Frelick slid across home plate to beat the throw from center fielder Jackson Merrill, the crowd let out a collective roar.

"I think it's probably in the top three of the special moments I've had in my career," Chourio said afterward.

FULL AT-BAT: Jackson Chourio vs. Mason Miller 🍿

The Brewers walk it off to take a 2-0 lead in the NLDS! pic.twitter.com/muBNJw1YKw

Since he made his Major League debut at just 20 years old, the Brewers have known that Chourio is special. After his first three seasons in the big leagues, with him already having monster postseason numbers, that bar might not be high enough. Milwaukee's young superstar is taking his game to an even higher level.

"I think he's been that type of player. The talent is undeniable when you watch him play," Yelich said of Chourio. "There's nothing he can't do on the baseball field. The more experience he gets, the more situations he's in, the more he kind of learns the league and just racks up the at-bats, he's just going to continue to get better.

"And that's kind of scary because he's pretty good right now."

Said Murphy: "He's starting to realize how he has to play the game. As talented as he is, he's still learning the game. … As a hitter, when he stays under control, it's amazing. He's, I think, turning into a bona fide, top-flight player. Couldn't be happier for him because he brings it every day."

With Chourio's heroics, the Brewers take a commanding 2-0 NLDS lead on the Padres and will head to San Diego one win away from returning to the NLCS. By winning a game Sunday in which they didn't play anywhere close to their best until the very end, this team showed that they can find a way no matter what.

"It's the attention to detail that is instilled in our culture, stuff that I learned from [Yelich] when I first got called up," Frelick said. "If you're not doing it, you don't play."

"It's a team that's unified," Chourio said. "We know what our strengths are, and we know how to support each other. … Everyone's supporting each other, and we know how to win."

title: Marquette Topples Creighton In Five Sets
description: The Golden Eagles scrape together enough points to beat the Bluejays on the road for the first time in over five years.
fullText:
And just like that, everyone in the Big East has one loss after four matches of conference play.

Sunday's Marquette/Creighton match was the last contest in the cycle to get everyone to four matches played. Going into Saturday's contests, we were down to Creighton and Butler with a zero in the loss column, and St. John's took care of business there, 3-1, leaving the Bluejays as the last unbeaten in the league as of Sunday morning.

And for a second there, probably several seconds there in Omaha, it looked like Creighton was going to be able to say that on Monday morning, too. The Bluejays took the first set from Marquette, 25-16, holding the Golden Eagles to just .114 hitting and rolling past them at a .343 clip. It was 5-0 Bluejays before anyone blinked, and MU couldn't get closer than three points. Another 5-0 run made it 20-12, and thus academic.

Creighton broke open some four point leads in the second set but Marquette was able to overcome those this time. It was tightly contested, all the way up to a misfire from Carson Tyler bringing the Jays within one, 23-22, but Caydence Doolan got the call and put down the final two points to even the match at one set each.

The Jays got out to a little lead early in the third, but this time Marquette wasn't quite as successful at powering through. The lead hit five, then six, then seven at 20-13, and yep, trouble town. The Golden Eagles scrapped together a few more points, but Ashlyn Paymal recorded a kill to make it 25-17, and that's two kind of lopsided Creighton wins against a hard fought Marquette win. That's a bad sign for a MU team that now needed to win the fourth in order to just get to a fifth set to try to beat the Jays. That's a bad sign for a Marquette team that hasn't done well when things have gone past three sets this season.

This time it was Marquette with the 4-0 lead out of the gate. That sounds encouraging, but Eloise Brandewie knotted the set at seven and an error by Tyler gave the Bluejays the lead. Tied at 10, then Marquette snapped off a 6-0 run. That was just enough space for Marquette to get to 25 before Creighton caught up with them, and an attack error by Ayden Ames gave the Golden Eagles the chance they needed.

Tied at 5, tied at 7, tied at 8, tied at 10, 11, 12, and 13. Remember, fifth set. First to 15, win by two. The last two ties, it was Creighton going up one and Marquette wiping it out on the next point.

Same thing again, tied at 14, extra points now required to win.

Same AGAIN, tied at 17. Four match points fended off by Marquette here.

Block by Luanna Markus and Julia Stanev… Marquette up 18-17?

S5 | MU 19 – Creighton 17

MU DEFEATS CREIGHTON ON THE ROAD IN 5 SETS!#WeAreMarquette | #MarquetteVB pic.twitter.com/Fzcfa2LfBJ

After a wild recovery free return from Creighton because of a Marquette rejection, Avery Helms camped underneath, sent it up to Markus for a swing from Tyler. She sent it hard into the Creighton block, which is not necessarily a good thing, but in this case, her shot went off the block, out of bounds on MU's side, Match Point Marquette, and the Golden Eagles have won a regularly timed regular season match at Creighton for the first time since 2011. It is just the eighth win in program history against Creighton, and it snaps a seven match winning streak in the series by the Bluejays.

And honestly? Marquette wasn't very good here. For the match, they hit just .160 against .286 from Creighton. All three of Marquette's hitters with more than 20 swings in the match hit under .160. Shouts to Molly Welge, who had eight kills and no errors on 19 attempts for a .421 day. Marquette couldn't do a thing to slow down Ashlyn Paymal or Eloise Brandewie, both of whom had 15+ kills and hit over .370. But they did close down Ayden Ames, who ended up hitting just .186 while tying with Abbey Hayes for the most swings from the Bluejays. Of note along the way here: Remember in the preview when I said that Trinity Shadd-Ceres was averaging a team high 3.05 kills and leading the team in total attacks, but she wasn't quite at that level last weekend?

Four swings while playing in all five sets. Hey, Creighton: Whatcha doin'?

How about some highlights, courtesy of GoMarquette.com and ESPN+?

Up Next: It's time for Marquette to play some home matches for the first time since September 20th. Next weekend's encounters will be against Georgetown at 7pm Central time on Friday and against Villanova at 5pm Central on Saturday, with ESPN+ taking the broadcast on both. Saturday's the big one, as it's the official ceremony for Tat Shiely and Allie Barber as the first two volleyball banners up in the McGuire Center.

The Hoyas are 10-5 on the year but 2-2 in the Big East after beating UConn and Providence at home this weekend, while the Wildcats are just 9-6 after starting the year earning AVCA top 25 votes, and they did exactly what Georgetown did to get to 2-2 in conference play.
